newsitem.title: USA: Republic Q3 hurt by weak selling prices.
newsitem.headline: Republic Q3 hurt by weak selling prices.

text.p: Republic Engineered Steels Inc said Wednesday that while shipping volume was up in the third quarter ended March 31, sales revenues fell by about $1.0 million to $196.6 million due to weaker selling prices.

It said, however, that despite the 15 percent decrease per ton in average selling price, gross profit for the quarter improved by 84 percent over the year earlier period because of a 17 percent increase in shipping volumes and 19 percent lower manufacturing costs.

The company also said cost of goods sold decreased 4.6 percent, even with higher shipments, as a result of high machinery utilization rates, decreased scrap and other raw materials costs, lower operating costs at its Cast-Roll facility and other cost reduction initiatives.
It also recorded a special pretax charge of $2.8 million for costs associated with reduction of its salaried workforce, it said.

For the latest quarter, Republic had an adjusted net loss of $3.081 million which excludes the after-tax effect of non-cash Employee Stock Ownership Plan charges and a onetime special charge for restructuring its salaried force.

Without the adjustment, the quarterly net loss amounted to $9.15 million, it said. For the same quarter a year ago, Republic had an adjusted net loss of $7.861 million, which excluded the after-tax effect of non-cash ESOP charges and a special charge for the closing of the company's eight-inch bar mill booked in that period.

Russell Maier, chairman and chief executive officer, said the company had significantly improved its performance from the same quarter a year ago and from last quarter,"but clearly it is not acceptable that we continue to sustain losses."
Continued cost improvements and product mix enhancements are beginning to pay off for the company, he said.
"However, pricing pressures and the need to lower costs on a permanent basis have been the major causes of the company's financial difficulties," he said.
Republic produces carbon and alloy high quality engineered bar, stainless, tool steels and remelted specialty steels.
